info.name: TalentPilot API — Auth, Accounts, Profiles, Resumes, Pipeline, Documents, Payments & Ops (Sprints 1-11)
info.description:
## Response envelope
Every 2xx response is `{ success: true, data, meta }`. Every error is `{ success: false, error: { code, message, details?, fields? }, meta }` — `code` is one of the `ErrorCode` values in `common/exceptions/app.exception.ts` (e.g. `INVALID_CREDENTIALS`, `OTP_EXPIRED`, `TOKEN_SUPERSEDED`, `PLAN_LIMIT_REACHED`, `RESUME_IN_USE`, `INSUFFICIENT_CREDITS`). `meta` always carries `requestId` + `timestamp`; paginated list endpoints also put `nextCursor`/`hasMore` in `meta` (not top-level).

## Auth model
- **Access token**: short-lived JWT (`JWT_ACCESS_TTL`, default 15m). Sent as `Authorization: Bearer <token>` — the collection auto-fills this from the `accessToken` variable, which Register/Verify/Login/Refresh test scripts populate automatically.
- **Refresh token**: opaque, rotating, lives in an httpOnly `tp_rt` cookie scoped to `/api/v1/auth`. Postman's cookie jar stores and resends it automatically like a browser — nothing to configure, just run requests in order within one Postman session.

## Suggested run order (folders are already in this order top to bottom)
1. **Register** → generates a fresh `{{email}}` each run, and grants `SIGNUP_CREDIT_GRANT` (100 by default) credits automatically
2. **Verify Email** → fill `otpCode` from the email/logs first (see its description for the dev caveat)
3. **Login** — alternative to step 2 if already verified; also works pre-verification
4. **Refresh Token** → rotates the session
5. **Get Me** / **Update Me**
6. **Get Profile** / **Update Profile**
7. **Upload Resume** (select a real PDF/DOCX in the `file` field) → captures `{{resumeId}}` → **List/Get/Rename/Download/Retry Resumes**
7b. Once `status` reaches `parsed` (extraction + AI parsing both run automatically on the worker), **List Resume Sections** → **Update Resume Section** to view/edit the extracted fields
8. **Paste Job Description** (or **Upload Job Description**) → captures `{{jdId}}`, analysed inline → **Score Resume Against Job Description** to match it against the resume from step 7 → **Delete Resume** / **Delete Job Description** last
9. **Workspaces & Pipeline**: **Create Workspace** (pairs `{{resumeId}}` + `{{jdId}}`) → **Start Analysis** → **Mint Stream Ticket** + **Live Progress (SSE)** (or just poll **Get Run Status** until `status` is `completed`/`partial`) → **Get ATS Report** for the actual score → **Retry Run** if it failed/partial → **Delete Workspace** last
10. Once the run is `completed`/`partial`, everything below reads from the SAME `{{workspaceId}}`/`{{resumeId}}` — no new setup needed: **Suggestions & Resume Versions** (list → apply/reject → diff/restore) → **Cover Letter** (get current, or regenerate for 2 credits) → **Interview Prep** (list questions → submit a practice answer for 1 credit) → **Company, Salary & Learning Roadmap** (all three are read-only GETs)
11. **List Sessions** / **Revoke Session** — do this *before* Logout, or the session you just revoked (Logout) won't be there to list
12. **Forgot Password** → fill `resetToken`, then **Reset Password**
13. **Logout** / **Delete Me** — destructive/terminal, kept last on purpose

## Resumes notes
- Upload requires a **verified** email and a free plan slot (max 3 resumes/user) — both surface as 403.
- Parsing is two automatic stages on the separate **worker** process (`pnpm start:worker`): text extraction (`uploaded` → `extracting` → `extracted`), then AI structuring (`extracted` → `parsing` → `parsed`). If a resume sits at `uploaded` or `extracted` forever, the worker isn't running, not a bug.
- AI structuring calls OpenAI (`OPENAI_API_KEY` required) and is metered/budget-capped (`AI_USER_DAILY_BUDGET_USD` / `AI_GLOBAL_DAILY_BUDGET_USD`) — a resume stuck at `parsing` with a 429/`AI_BUDGET_EXCEEDED` in `parseError` means the budget or kill switch, not a bug either.
- **Sections** (`personal_info`, `summary`, `skills`, `experience`, `projects`, `education`, `certifications`, `languages`) only exist once `status` is `parsed`. Editing a section via **Update Resume Section** marks it `editedByUser: true` so it survives a future re-parse.

## Job descriptions & matching notes
- Job descriptions are analysed **inline** (not queued) — the paste/upload response already carries `status: analyzed` with parsed requirements and skills, typically within a few seconds.
- Pasting/uploading text that normalizes to the same content hash for the same user returns the existing analysed row instead of paying for a second AI call.
- **Score Resume Against Job Description** requires the resume to be `parsed` and the JD to be `analyzed` first — otherwise it 409s with `RESUME_NOT_PARSED` or `JD_NOT_ANALYZED`.
- Re-running a match after editing neither side is free: embeddings are content-hashed per chunk, so unchanged chunks are reused (`stats.resume.reused` / `stats.jd.reused`) instead of re-embedded.
- Storage is MinIO locally (`docker compose up -d minio`) — the same code talks to real AWS S3 or Cloudflare R2 in other environments.

## Workspaces & pipeline notes (Sprints 5-8)
- A **workspace** pairs one resume with one job description. **Start Analysis** runs both through a 12-step DAG on the **worker** process:
  ```
  parse_resume ─┬─► generate_embeddings ─► match_keywords ─► score_ats ─┬─► optimize_resume ─► generate_cover_letter ─┐
                │                                                       └─► build_learning_path ───────────────────┤
  parse_jd ─────┼─► research_company     (optional)                                                                 ├─► finalize
                ├─► estimate_salary      (optional)                                                                 │
                └─► generate_interview_qs ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
  ```
  `research_company`/`estimate_salary`/`generate_interview_qs` don't need the ATS score, so they run CONCURRENTLY with the whole scoring branch — a full run finishes in roughly 45-90s, not the ~3min it would take serialised. Every step is idempotent, so a crashed/retried run never redoes (or recharges for) completed work.
- Costs a flat **21 credits** (was 10 pre-Sprint-7), debited atomically with creating the run; requires a unique `Idempotency-Key` header (use Postman's `{{$guid}}` dynamic variable) so a retried request replays the existing run instead of double-charging.
- Only one active (`queued`/`running`) run per workspace — enforced by a database partial unique index, not just application logic, so it holds even under concurrent requests. A second **Start Analysis** call while one is active 409s `ANALYSIS_ALREADY_RUNNING`.
- `research_company` and `estimate_salary` are optional (`required: false`) — a dead Tavily key or a JD with no company name leaves the run `partial` with everything else intact, never `failed`. A failed optional step no longer blocks `finalize` (which depends on every step, optional ones included) from still running.
- Progress is pushed live via SSE (**Mint Stream Ticket** then **Live Progress (SSE)**), or pollable via **Get Run Status** — both share the same state shape. A run that partially fails (`status: partial`) proportionally refunds credits for the steps that didn't complete; **Retry Run** re-runs only the failed/blocked steps for free.
- The worker process (`pnpm start:worker`) must be running for any of this to progress past `queued` — same caveat as resume/JD parsing above.

## Optimisation, cover letter & career-prep notes (Sprints 7-8)
- **Suggestions** (from `optimize_resume`) go through a fabrication guard in code, not just prompt rules — invented metrics, years, employers/schools, and credentials are silently dropped before they ever reach **List Suggestions**. What you see has already passed verification.
- **Apply Suggestions** batches every accepted suggestion into ONE new resume version (not one version per suggestion) and is free — already paid for by the run that generated them. If you hand-edit a bullet via the Sections API *after* a suggestion for it was generated, applying that suggestion is refused (`skipped`, marked `stale`) rather than silently overwriting your edit.
- Resume history is append-only: **Restore Resume Version** copies an old version FORWARD as a new one — it never rewrites or deletes anything, so you can always get back to where you were. **Diff Resume Versions** is word-level, not character-level, so a one-word change doesn't read as unreadable noise.
- **Cover Letter** is generated automatically by the run; **Regenerate Cover Letter** is a separate on-demand action (different tone/length) that costs 2 credits — but only on success: your balance is checked before the AI is even called, and the debit itself only happens after a clean result (no `[Company Name]`-style placeholders), so a rejected generation is never charged.
- **Interview Prep** questions are grounded in this candidate's actual resume and this JD's actual requirements — `basedOn` names what prompted each one. **Submit Practice Answer** follows the same charge-only-on-success rule as cover letter regeneration: 1 credit, checked and debited around the AI call, never charged for a failure.
- **Company Insight** is cached globally for 7 days per (normalised) company name — the 50th person who applies to the same company this week gets a free, already-computed answer (`fromCache: true`). `confidence: "low"` is an honest signal the company has little public information, not an error.
- **Salary Estimate** is always a range (`p25`/`p50`/`p75`) with `isEstimate: true` baked into the entity itself — there is no code path that returns a bare number.
- **Learning Roadmap** is capped at 6 items (enforced by the prompt AND in code) — a longer list reads as a guilt trip, not a plan.

Import `TalentPilot-API.postman_environment.json` alongside this collection and select it as your active environment before running anything.

request.description:
Creates an unverified account and emails a 6-digit OTP (see `verify-email`). Deliberately returns 409 if the email is already registered — that surface is defended by rate limiting (5/min/IP), not by lying, so the frontend can tell the user their email is taken. Password needs at least one letter and one digit, 8-72 chars.

**Dev note:** with a placeholder `RESEND_API_KEY` in `.env`, the verification email will fail to send and the OTP job will retry and eventually die in BullMQ — there is currently no way to read the code back out short of a real Resend key or a temporary log statement in `OtpService.issueOtp`. Configure a real key to exercise `verify-email` end to end.

response.name: 409 Conflict — email already registered
400 Bad Request — weak password

request.description: Consumes the 6-digit OTP and logs you straight in — set `otpCode` from the email before running this. Idempotent for an already-verified account (just logs in). On success, sets the `tp_rt` httpOnly refresh cookie (Postman stores it automatically) and returns an access token.

response.name: 400 Bad Request — wrong code

request.description: Always returns 204, even for an unknown or already-verified email — existence is never revealed. Subject to a per-account cooldown (`OTP_RESEND_COOLDOWN_SEC`, default 60s) on top of the 3/min/IP rate limit.

Unverified users can still log in (VerifiedGuard blocks specific routes separately). Unknown email and wrong password return an identical 401 body in identical time — no user-enumeration oracle. Rate limited to 5/min/IP. Sets the `tp_rt` refresh cookie.

No body — reads the `tp_rt` httpOnly cookie set by Register/Verify/Login, which Postman's cookie jar sends automatically as long as you've run one of those first in this session. Rotates the token and returns a new access token. Two concurrent refreshes with the same token are a race, not theft: the loser gets a soft 401 `TOKEN_SUPERSEDED` and should retry with its current token, not log out. A token replayed long after rotation is treated as theft and the whole device family is revoked (`TOKEN_INVALID`).

response.name: 401 Unauthorized — no/invalid/expired cookie
401 Unauthorized — concurrent refresh race (soft, retry)

request.description: "Who am I" — the frontend calls this on every app load.

Placeholder: the users table has no self-editable columns yet, so this always returns the account unchanged (see `UpdateUserDto`). `forbidNonWhitelisted` rejects any body property you send here, so keep the body an empty object. Password changes go through the auth reset flow, never this endpoint.
Returns an empty shell (every field `null`, `completeness: 0`) if the user has never saved a profile — this is never a 404, so the frontend's settings form always has something to bind to.

request.description: A foreign id (belongs to another user) 404s — never 403, which would confirm the resource exists.

The API never streams file bytes itself — this 302-redirects to a short-lived `SIGNED_URL_TTL_SEC` (default 15min) presigned URL that the browser/client fetches directly from storage.

**Auto-follow-redirect is disabled on this request on purpose.** The presigned URL IS the auth for that request — MinIO/S3 reject it if an unrelated `Authorization: Bearer ...` header rides along, which Postman/Newman would otherwise attach since it forwards headers across redirects by default even to a completely different host. Expect a `302` here with a `Location` header; copy that URL into a new tab (or a fresh request with no auth) to actually fetch the file.
Only valid when status is `failed` — resets to `uploaded` and re-queues text extraction on the worker.

response.name: 200 OK

request.description: Soft delete. Blocked with 409 if any workspace still references this resume — the error body lists exactly which ones, so it is actionable instead of a dead end. **Destructive** — run after the other Resumes requests, not before.

response.name: 409 Conflict — RESUME_IN_USE

request.description: Returns the AI-extracted sections for a resume (personal_info, summary, skills, experience, projects, education, certifications, languages), in display order. Empty until the AI parse job (queued automatically after text extraction) has completed — check the resume's `status` first; it must be `parsed`.

response.name: 200 OK

request.description: Overwrites one section's content. The URL segment is the section type: personal_info, summary, skills, experience, projects, education, certifications, or languages — each has its own content shape (object for personal_info/summary, array for the rest). Content is validated against that shape before saving; a mismatch returns 400 VALIDATION_FAILED. Marks the section as user-edited so a future re-parse will not overwrite it.

Embeds both sides (skipping any chunk whose content is unchanged since the last call — free on a re-run), then returns a calibrated 0-100 semantic score per requirement plus a keyword coverage report. The resume must be `parsed` and the job description `analyzed` first.

request.description: Pairs a resume with a job description so they can be run through the analysis pipeline together. `resumeId`/`jobDescriptionId` must both belong to the current user — a foreign or unknown id 404s (never 403). response.name: 201 Created

request.description: Cursor-paginated, newest first. Pass the previous page's `meta.nextCursor` as `?cursor=` to continue.

request.description:
Starts (or resumes) a full analysis run: parse resume → parse JD → generate embeddings → match keywords → score against ATS criteria. Requires a **verified** email and a unique `Idempotency-Key` header (Postman's `{{$guid}}` dynamic variable fills a fresh one each send — replaying the same key returns the same run instead of starting, and charging for, a second one). Debits 10 credits atomically with creating the run; every new account is granted `SIGNUP_CREDIT_GRANT` (100 by default) on registration, so a fresh account can run this ~10 times before topping up.

Only one active run per workspace at a time — a second call while one is `queued`/`running` 409s with `ANALYSIS_ALREADY_RUNNING` instead of racing it.

After this returns, either open **Live Progress (SSE)** or poll **Get Run Status**.

response.name: 400 Bad Request — missing Idempotency-Key
402 Payment Required — insufficient credits
409 Conflict — resume/JD not ready
409 Conflict — analysis already running

request.description: The browser's `EventSource` API can't send an `Authorization` header, so the stream endpoint below authenticates via a single-use, 60-second ticket instead of a Bearer token. Call this (authenticated normally) first, then open **Live Progress (SSE)** with the returned ticket before it expires.

Server-Sent Events — `text/event-stream`, not a normal JSON response, so this request is here for reference/documentation more than for Postman's response viewer (which buffers the whole thing rather than rendering it live). Auth is the single-use ticket from **Mint Stream Ticket** in the query string, not a Bearer token — this route is `@Public()`.

Always sends a `snapshot` event first (current state), so a client that connects after the run already finished still gets a useful response instead of waiting forever; then `run.started`/`step.*`/`run.completed`/`run.failed` events as they happen, plus a `ping` heartbeat every 15s. To watch it live outside Postman:

```
curl -N "{{baseUrl}}/workspaces/runs/{{runId}}/stream?ticket={{streamTicket}}"
```

response.name: 200 OK — text/event-stream
401 Unauthorized — expired/invalid/already-consumed ticket

request.description: Polling fallback for clients that skip SSE — same state shape as the SSE `snapshot` event.

response.name: 200 OK — completed
200 OK — partial (one optional step failed)

request.description: The actual score — the output of the most recent completed `score_ats` step for this workspace: `overallScore`, the seven-component breakdown with the exact weight/contribution of each (so the UI can show its work, not just a bare number), AI-written strengths/weaknesses/recommendations, and the full keyword match list. Only meaningful once the workspace's `status` (from **Get Workspace** / **Get Run Status**) is `completed` or has a report despite being `partial` — otherwise 409s with `REPORT_NOT_READY`.

response.name: 200 OK

response.name: 409 Conflict — no completed analysis yet

request.description: Only valid for a `failed` or `partial` run — completed steps are skipped (StepRunner is idempotent), so this only re-does the work that actually failed, and does **not** re-charge credits.

response.name: 200 OK

request.description: Soft delete — kept last in this folder since it's destructive/terminal, same convention as Delete Resume/Delete Job Description.

AI-generated resume-optimisation suggestions from the `optimize_resume` pipeline step. Every suggestion has already passed the fabrication guard — invented metrics, years, organisations, and credentials are dropped silently before they ever reach this list.

response.name: 200 OK

request.description: Accepts a batch of suggestions as ONE new resume version — not one version per suggestion, which would make the history unreadable. A suggestion is refused (marked `stale`, returned in `skipped`) if the underlying bullet was hand-edited since the suggestion was generated; the user's edit always wins and is never silently overwritten. Free — no credits charged (already paid for by the analysis run that generated them).

response.name: 201 Created — one suggestion refused as stale

request.description: Dismisses a batch of suggestions without applying them — no new resume version is created.
Newest first. v1 is always the original upload — applying suggestions or restoring an older version always creates a NEW version forward, so history is never rewritten.

response.name: 200 OK

request.description: Word-level diff per section (not character-level, which turns a one-word change into unreadable noise). Only sections that actually changed are returned.

response.name: 200 OK

request.description: Copies the target version FORWARD as a new version — restoring v1 when you're on v3 creates v4, it does not delete v2/v3. History is never rewritten, so you can always come back.

response.name: 404 Not Found — that version does not exist

request.description: The cover letter produced by the pipeline's `generate_cover_letter` step (or the most recent **Regenerate**, whichever is newer).

response.name: 200 OK

request.description: Regenerates with a different tone (`professional` | `friendly` | `confident` | `enthusiastic`) and/or length (`short` | `standard` | `long`), both optional. Costs 2 credits and supersedes the previous version as current — the old one stays in the history for reference. Balance is checked, and the AI called, BEFORE any credit is debited: a generation that fails (e.g. the placeholder guard rejects a `[Company Name]`-style output) is never charged.

response.name: 201 Created
402 Payment Required — insufficient credits

request.description: Generated by `generate_interview_qs`, which runs in parallel with the ATS scoring branch (it only needs the parsed resume + JD, not the score). Mixed by type (`hr` | `behavioral` | `technical` | `coding` | `system_design`) and difficulty, grounded in this candidate's actual experience — `basedOn` names the resume item or JD requirement that prompted each question.

response.name: 200 OK

request.description: Practice mode: costs 1 credit per attempt, only charged if the AI feedback call actually succeeds (checked against your balance first, so a request you can't afford never spends real OpenAI money).

request.description: Tavily-grounded company research from `research_company` (optional step — Tavily/no-company-name failures leave this 404 rather than failing the whole run). Globally cached for 7 days per company (by normalised name), so the 50th person researching the same company pays nothing and gets the same answer — `fromCache: true` on a hit. `confidence: "low"` with a thin `overview` means the company genuinely has little public information, not a bug; every claim is traceable via `sources`.

response.name: 200 OK
404 Not Found — research didn't run or is still pending

request.description: From `estimate_salary` (optional step). Always a range (`p25`/`p50`/`p75`) with `isEstimate: true` — the API never returns a single figure or presents this as a quote. `methodology` states what it's actually based on.

GDPR soft delete: blocks login immediately, revokes every session, sets `deletedAt`. The account is excluded from normal queries but kept for a 30-day grace window before a scheduled hard purge (see GdprService.purgeExpired, Sprint 11) that also cancels any active Stripe subscription and deletes S3 objects. **Destructive for this test user** — run it last.

Queues generation of a document. `type` is one of `resume_pdf` | `resume_docx` | `cover_letter_pdf` | `cover_letter_docx` | `full_report_pdf`. Rendering happens worker-side (Puppeteer for PDFs, the `docx` package for Word files) — poll **Get Document Status** until `status` is `ready`, then call **Download Document**. Every call creates a NEW row (never reuses an existing one), so the returned id is always this specific request's document.

request.description: **Not callable from Postman** — this endpoint verifies the raw request body against the `Stripe-Signature` header using `STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET`; a hand-built Postman body will always 400 with `WEBHOOK_SIGNATURE_INVALID`. To exercise it locally, run `stripe listen --forward-to localhost:3000/api/v1/payments/webhook` and `stripe trigger checkout.session.completed` (or `invoice.payment_succeeded` / `invoice.payment_failed` / `customer.subscription.updated`) from the Stripe CLI. Idempotent (a replayed `event.id` is skipped) and safe against out-of-order delivery.

Deliberately checks NO dependency — proves only that the process itself is responsive. A Postgres/Redis outage should page someone, not trigger a container-restart storm on every replica; that's what readiness is for.

Pings Postgres and Redis. Returns the raw Terminus health-check shape (NOT the usual {success,data,meta} envelope) — 503s if either dependency is unreachable. A deploy should gate on this; a load balancer should stop routing to an instance failing it.
One batched round-trip (credit balance, plan, resume/workspace counts, recent workspaces, unread notifications) — cached in Redis for 30s per user.
SUM of the append-only credit ledger for the current user.
